section_summary: This section contains State Department records from 1938 to 1944 focusing on Japanese governmental organization, cabinet changes, wartime administrative centralization, and anti-militarist movements. Prominent topics include the emergence of the Jushin (senior statesmen) council to replace the Genro, total-war industrial reorganizations including the Armament Ministry and Supreme War Directing Council, and the political fallout of Allied victories culminating in the fall of the Tojo Cabinet. The file also chronicles activities of anti-fascist Japanese groups in the United States and the Chinese Communist base of Yenan, notably the Japanese American Committee for Democracy and Susumu Okano's Japanese People's Emancipation League.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a Tokyo despatch concerning the establishment of Japan's new Genro advisory body.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 4917 on a new advisory body replacing the Genro in selecting prime ministers.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japan's New Genro

subfiles.about: Diplomatic report analyzing the emergence of the Jushin council of senior statesmen replacing the Genro in selecting Japanese prime ministers.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits an analytical report based partly on an article by Dr. Masamichi Royama in Contemporary Japan. The despatch reviews how the assassination of Premier Inukai in 1932 and military aggression in Manchuria ended party government and diminished the role of Prince Saionji, the last surviving Genro. It explains the development of the Jushin body, composed of the Lord Privy Seal, the President of the Privy Council, and former prime ministers, who now deliberate on cabinet selections under significant military influence.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4917: Japan's New Genro

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting conversations regarding Japanese-Chinese peace negotiations and domestic cabinet instability.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1171: Chungking negotiations on recognizing the Wang Ching-wei regime; Ushiba blames Konoye and Matsuoka for the German pact.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Negotiations with Chungking Govt for Recognition of Wang Ching Wei Govt

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording diplomatic observations on the political uncertainty of the Konoye Government.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Vichy Telegram No. 1039: instability in Tokyo and difficulty identifying a successor to Prince Konoye.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Government of Japan

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum comparing the administrative abilities and civil service backgrounds of Japanese and American public officials.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine says Japanese officials compare unfavorably in ability with American ones, owing to narrow experience and secure tenure, but are devoted, tactful and tenacious; Saionji and Hara were exceptions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Comparative Ability of Japanese and American Public Officials

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding rumored disagreements within the Japanese Cabinet over the Tripartite Pact.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 765: rumored split between Konoye and Matsuoka, denied by Matsumoto.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Rumored Cleavage Between Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum analyzing Axis recognition of the Wang Ching-wei puppet regime in Nanking.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck argues German and Italian recognition of Wang Ching-wei will not help Japan with Chinese, since Italy admitted acting at Japan's request, confirming Wang's puppet status.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: German and Italian Recognition of Wang Ching-wei

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet documenting high-level departmental discussions on a newly formed Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telephone conversation between Maxwell Hamilton and the Secretary of State about the new government set up in Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: New Government Set Up by Japanese

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet reporting the resignation of the Japanese Ambassador to the Soviet Union and the designation of his successor.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1188: Ambassador Tatekawa resigned February 28, 1942; Naotake Sato to succeed him in Moscow.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Resignation of Japanese Ambassador Tatekawa

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet concerning press statements on petroleum export restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a memorandum on revising press releases on petroleum export controls, citing U.S. defense needs without naming Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Restrictions on Exports of Petroleum Products

subfiles.about: Letter acknowledging the receipt of informational pamphlets concerning Japan.
subfiles.summary: George Atcheson Jr. thanks Juanita Miller of Los Angeles for three pamphlets on Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to Juanita Miller Acknowledging Pamphlets on Japan

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing material on Japanese industrial reorganization and rationalization.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a letter on the Rational Plan for the Reorganization of Japan and industrial rationalization.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Rational Plan for the Reorganization of Japan

subfiles.about: Telegraphic resolution of loyalty to the United States sent by Japanese American citizens in Oregon.
subfiles.from: Portland Chapter, Japanese American Citizens League
subfiles.summary: The Portland Chapter of the Japanese American Citizens League transmits a resolution adopted at a patriotic rally on January 23, 1942. The assembled residents reaffirm their loyalty to the United States and pledge their services and resources to defeat Japan and its Axis partners.
subfiles.title: Telegram: JACL Patriotic Rally Resolution of Loyalty

subfiles.about: Correspondence between the Japanese American Committee for Democracy and the State Department regarding anti-fascist coordination.
subfiles.summary: Takagi of the JACD commends the State Department's role at a Cleveland conference and offers cooperation; Hoskins thanks him on May 21 for his letter and newsletter.
subfiles.title: Correspondence Between JACD and Executive Assistant Hoskins

subfiles.about: Internal memoranda and correspondence concerning a testimonial letter of loyalty presented to the President by the JACD.
subfiles.from: Toshi Aline Ohta / Division of Protocol / Edwin M. Watson
subfiles.summary: This dossier documents the handling of a testimonial of loyalty sent to President Roosevelt by Toshi Aline Ohta on behalf of the Japanese American Committee for Democracy. The White House referred the document to the State Department, where the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Division of Protocol recommended a presidential acknowledgment. The file concludes with a draft and signed acknowledgment from Major General Edwin M. Watson, Secretary to the President, expressing appreciation for the testimonial.
subfiles.title: Dossier: JACD Testimonial of Loyalty and Presidential Acknowledgment

subfiles.about: Military intelligence request for State Department documentation on Japanese military government administration in the Dutch East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Lt. Col. Adams asks for State Department data on Japanese occupation administration, especially the Dutch East Indies, for the School of Military Government.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Japanese Military Government in Japanese-held Territory

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a memorandum on the de facto structure of the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to John K. Emmerson's memorandum Japan's Govt. in Fact.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Japan's Govt. in Fact

subfiles.about: Correspondence and memorandum discussing a proposal to distribute a Japanese translation of Joseph C. Grew's book in Brazil.
subfiles.from: Yoshitaka Takagi / Allan Dawson / John C. Dreier
subfiles.summary: Takagi of the JACD plans a Japanese translation of Grew's Report from Tokyo and asks about distributing it in Brazil; Dawson and Dreier advise against official promotion and suggest other channels.
subfiles.title: Correspondence: Distribution of 'Report from Tokyo' Translation in Brazil

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram and paraphrase assessing Premier Tojo's announced wartime emergency measures and Allied strategic pressures.
subfiles.summary: Winant relays British views: Tojo's emergency measures respond to Italy's surrender and Pacific setbacks, with no immediate government collapse expected, and rhetoric shifting from expansion to defense of the home islands.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6380: British Foreign Office Analysis of Tojo Emergency Measures

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram detailing German reports on Japanese wartime administrative reorganization and the creation of an Armament Ministry.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports German news of a centralized Japanese Armament Ministry, a planned Commerce and Agriculture Ministry, military officers replacing civilian bureaucrats, and Wohlthat's survey of occupied China.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6381: Japanese Administrative Changes and Armament Ministry

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting German editorial commentary on the leadership of the new Japanese Armament Ministry and Nobusuke Kishi.
subfiles.summary: German commentary on merging the Planning Bureau and Economics Ministry into an Armament Ministry: Kishi will be deputy and guiding figure, while Tojo or another officer is expected to hold the portfolio.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6529: German Commentary on Japanese Armament Ministry and Kishi

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram transmitting German press accounts of new Japanese legislation creating industrial 'production generals.'
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports Japan's new armament law making companies and designated production generals responsible for war output; the Armament Ministry controls prices, financing, accounting and labor.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7264: Japanese Armament Legislation and Production Generals

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram summarizing German press reports on the internal reorganization of Japan's Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports German coverage of the Greater East Asia Ministry's December 1, 1943 reorganization, absorbing commercial and industrial functions into a new Industrial Department.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7877: Reorganization of Greater East Asia Ministry

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting Tojo's directives to major Japanese war industries and a major wartime tax increase.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports Tojo told 150 leading firms to name responsible managers under the armament law within two weeks, stressing aircraft; a new tax program aims to raise two billion yen.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 502: Tojo Directives to Armament Industries and New Tax Program

subfiles.about: Military intelligence follow-up requesting a consular dispatch on Japanese military government methods.
subfiles.summary: Lt. Col. Adams requests Consul General Foote's Despatch No. 15 (January 14, 1943) on Japanese military government for the School of Military Government.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Despatch Desired by School of Military Government

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum proposing policy options should the Japanese Emperor flee to the Asian continent and abdicate.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine proposes that an Emperor's flight to the continent be declared voluntary abdication, leaving the Allies free to enthrone another prince or abolish the throne, with great propaganda value.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Proposed Policy on Contingency of Emperor's Flight

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum warning of the possible flight of the Japanese imperial court and high command to China.
subfiles.summary: Breckinridge Long warns Grew that Japan's leaders and Royal Family might flee to inland China, where large armies and puppet regimes could form a redoubt, and urges contingency planning.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Contingency of Japanese Flight to Continental China

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting British press analysis on the fall of the Tojo Cabinet and appointment of Koiso and Yonai.
subfiles.summary: Winant summarizes British press on Tojo's fall after Saipan, seeing Koiso and Yonai's selection as inter-service conflict and noting shipping losses and a shift from conquest to home defense.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 5814: British Press Commentary on Tojo's Fall and New Cabinet

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting leadership changes in the Imperial Rule Assistance Political Association.
subfiles.summary: Harriman relays that Admiral Seizo Kobayashi agreed to head the Imperial Rule Assistance Political Association, replacing General Nobuyuki Abe, who became Governor General of Korea.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2911: Leadership Change in Imperial Rule Assistance Association

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum and press clipping analyzing the formation of Japan's Supreme War Directing Council.
subfiles.summary: Benninghoff rebuts Kawakami's claim that the Supreme War Directing Council shifts blame to civilians: it replaces the Liaison Council to bridge civil government and Supreme Command for total war, not surrender.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: The Japanese Supreme War Directing Council

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting an observer report on the Japanese People's Emancipation League at Yenan and a speech by Susumu Okano.
subfiles.summary: Gauss transmits John Service's report on the Japanese People's Emancipation League at Yenan, with Okano's August 12, 1944 address appealing for Allied recognition and outlining a postwar democratic republic.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2981: Report on Japanese People's Emancipation League at Yenan

subfiles.about: Military headquarters despatch transmitting Service's report and Okano's Yenan address to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: John Paton Davies forwards Service's report, calling the League the only significant Free Japan movement, worth study for invasion planning and postwar governance, with Okano's speech attached.
subfiles.title: Despatch: Transmitting Report on Japanese People's Emancipation League

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting a proposal from Susumu Okano to the JACD in New York to form a unified Japanese people's front.
subfiles.summary: Ringwalt forwards Okano's letter to the JACD's Takagi proposing a joint committee and a U.S.-based League headquarters; Davies sees an invitation for American influence on postwar Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3160: Transmission of Letter from Susumu Okano to JACD

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing an article on Korea for the Harvard Civil Affairs Training School.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to correspondence enclosing Hugh Borton's article on Korea for Harvard's Civil Affairs Training School.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Article on Korea for Harvard CATS
subfiles.to: Civil Affairs Training School, Harvard University

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Hugh Borton's study on Korean internal political structure.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Northwestern University letter enclosing Hugh Borton's paper on Korea's internal political structure.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference: Article on Korea Internal Political Structure

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum recommending the disapproval of Japanese naval inspector assignments to Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Coville recommends rejecting expansion of Japanese naval offices beyond New York to Los Angeles and denying tax exemptions, citing Navy objections and public hostility.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Japanese Naval Inspector's Office Personnel in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum summarizing records of foreign military and naval purchasing missions in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Coville lists foreign military purchasing offices with fixed U.S. locations (Japan, France, Britain, Australia) and 28 countries with traveling missions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Foreign Military and Naval Offices in the United States
